bullets: Culture is a system that never sits still—its dynamic nature must be acknowledged rather than resisted.
Cultural drift cannot be gripped or controlled directly; it must be noticed and responded to through awareness.
The second-order effect of cultural drift is the part most people overlook, yet it shapes long-term outcomes.
Dialogue and cultural drift intersect when teams recognize patterns across time, not just in moment-to-moment interactions.
Systems thinking reveals trade-offs that cross-cut all aspects of cultural and organizational behavior.
Ignoring cultural drift leads to rebuilding the same structures from scratch a year later.
Running an idea for two weeks enables iteration and reveals whether it holds across time and context.
The act of noticing drift—rather than forcing control—is the core skill in navigating cultural change.
